summary: Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a Master of Arts at Australian National University around 1980–1983, supervised by Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.

Ann Gleig specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University (~2004–2010) under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey J. Kripal and committee members William B. Parsons and James D. Faubion.

Ann Grodzins Gold is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago (~1972–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993–2021) as Professor of Religion and Anthropology.

Ann Heirman is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009). From 2003 to 2012, she served at Ghent University as professor of Chinese language and culture and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Ann Laura Stoler works in history, archaeology, and other fields, having studied at Columbia University (~1972–1982). She held academic posts at the University of Michigan (1989–2003) and The New School (2004).

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (MA, through 1998), Heidelberg University, and the University of Würzburg. Around 2006, she served as Assistant Professor to the Chair of Indology at the University of Würzburg.

Anna Balikci Denjongpa specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Supervised by Lionel Caplan, she earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (~1995–2002), and in 2002 became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She was a member of IsMEO (1984), directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003), lectured at University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2013), and held a post at University of Naples Federico II (~2017).

Anna M. Gade is a religious studies scholar who held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (~2004–2012) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she became Associate Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia around 2012.
Anna M. Shields is a scholar of Sinology. She held an academic post at the University of Maryland, College Park from around 2007 to 2015 and began a post at Princeton University around 2015.

Anna Madelyn Hennessey specializes in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2005–2011) under doctoral supervisor William F. Powell, with Ronald Egan and Richard D. Hecht serving on her committee.

Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna (~2006–2012) under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and a PhD at Heidelberg University (~2013–2018) under supervisors Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer.
Anna Seidel was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Between approximately 1961 and 1968, she studied under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein.
Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1972–1976). She held academic posts at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1990–1999) and New York University (~1999).

Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University by 2007, under the supervision of Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada.

Anne Carolyn Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who studied at Wisconsin-Madison and Virginia. She taught at Harvard (~1987–1989), chaired Religious Studies at Rice (1994), and co-founded the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.

Anne Casile works in Indology and archaeology. She served as an Arts and Humanities Research Council research assistant at the British Museum (~2008–2011) and held a post at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development starting around 2012.

Anne E. Monius was a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned her degree at Harvard (~1989–1997) under Charles Hallisey. She held posts at the University of Virginia (~1997–2002) and Harvard University as professor of South Asian religions (2002).

Anne Feldhaus is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at Manhattanville University (~1967–1971) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976), later holding a post at Arizona State University around 1981.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1991–1999), and held a Redaktionsråd post at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.
